title: OpenAI Picks Foxconn's FIH Mobile to Build First AI Phone
summary: OpenAI's first phone lands at Foxconn FIH Mobile. Custom 2nm MediaTek chip, dual AI processors. Late 2027 launch for builders chasing platform independence.

# OpenAI Picks Foxconn's FIH Mobile to Build First AI Phone


By OpenTools Team


·


November 20, 2026


Foxconn subsidiary FIH Mobile locked in the assembly order for OpenAI's first phone, packing a custom 2nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600 with dual AI processors. Three other Apple suppliers feed the component pipeline. Mass production targets late 2027 or 2028, a direct shot at breaking free from Google and Apple platforms.


## Foxconn Wins the Assembly Gig


Foxconn subsidiary **FIH Mobile** has landed the assembly order for[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's first smartphone, Chinese outlet *Securities Times* reported this week, citing supply chain sources. The[Android Authority](https://www.androidauthority.com/openai-phone-foxconn-assembly-3737193/) confirmed the report independently through its own supply chain checks. Neither OpenAI nor Foxconn has issued an official statement. FIH Mobile — a Foxconn unit listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange — designs, manufactures, and assembles phones for multiple brands. The two companies already partner on AI data center equipment, and Foxconn Chairman Young Liu said in late October 2026 that discussions about "additional joint projects" were underway, according to[Gadgets360](https://www.gadgets360.com/mobiles/news/openai-ai-phone-assembly-manufacturing-partner-launch-timeline-report-12352522) .


## Under the Hood: The Spec Sheet


Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo laid out the hardware[blueprint](https://opentools.ai/tools/blueprint) months ago. Here is what builders should care about:


MediaTek appears to be the exclusive chip supplier, edging out Qualcomm for this socket,[Android Authority](https://www.androidauthority.com/openai-phone-foxconn-assembly-3737193/) reports. Kuo previously estimated 30 million units across 2027 and 2028 if development stays on track.


- **Custom 2nm MediaTek Dimensity 9600** Built on TSMC's next-gen node, per[Gadgets360](https://www.gadgets360.com/mobiles/news/openai-ai-phone-assembly-manufacturing-partner-launch-timeline-report-12352522)


- **Two dedicated AI processing units** Separate silicon just for on-device inference


- **LPDDR6 RAM** The fastest mobile memory standard available


- **UFS 5.0 storage** Double the bandwidth of UFS 4.0 for model loading


- **Camera hardware tuned for AI** Sensors designed to help the model understand physical surroundings, not just take photos


## The Apple Supply Chain Moves In


[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) is not building a supply chain from scratch. It is renting Apple's. Beyond FIH Mobile, three other Apple suppliers are feeding the component pipeline:


- **Luxshare Precision** — once tipped as the exclusive manufacturing partner by Ming-Chi Kuo, now reportedly handling component supply instead of final assembly, per[Android Authority](https://www.androidauthority.com/openai-phone-foxconn-assembly-3737193/)
- **Lingyi iTech** — structural and thermal components
- **AAC Technologies** — acoustic and haptic parts


The shift from Luxshare as exclusive partner to FIH Mobile as assembler suggests OpenAI is diversifying risk.[EE Times](https://www.eetimes.com/openai-prepares-ai-first-smartphone-for-2028/) noted earlier that Luxshare would serve as co-design and manufacturing partner, but the latest reports from *Securities Times* and *Cailian Press* paint a wider supplier net.


## Agents Replace the App Grid


The hardware is only half the story. The real bet is software. Instead of a[grid](https://opentools.ai/tools/grid) of app icons,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's phone runs **AI agents that complete tasks directly** — no app-switching required. Ming-Chi Kuo shared a concept visualization showing an "agent task stream" replacing the traditional home screen,[The Decoder](https://the-decoder.com/openais-first-hardware-play-might-be-a-phone-that-replaces-your-app-grid-with-an-agent-task-stream/) reported. "Instead of apps, the smartphone could rely on AI agents to complete different tasks," Kuo wrote in his original analyst note, cited by[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/27/openai-could-be-making-a-phone-with-ai-agents-replacing-apps/) . The phone runs a mix of small on-device models for latency-sensitive tasks and cloud models for heavier lifting. OpenAI's pitch: a phone that understands context continuously, anticipates what you need, and acts without making you tap through six apps.


## The OS Wildcard


Nobody knows what operating system this thing runs. A **customized Android fork** is the obvious starting point — it brings an existing app ecosystem and developer tools. Building from scratch offers total control but[zero](https://opentools.ai/tools/zero-language) apps on day one.[Android Authority](https://www.androidauthority.com/openai-phone-foxconn-assembly-3737193/) calls the OS "unknown" and notes the tradeoff clearly: "A customized version of Android is considered a natural starting point due to its app ecosystem. Building an OS from scratch would offer more freedom but face adoption challenges." For builders, the OS choice determines everything about the development surface. If it is Android-based, the SDK story gets easier. If it is proprietary,[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) needs to ship a developer platform alongside the hardware. The[EE Times](https://www.eetimes.com/openai-prepares-ai-first-smartphone-for-2028/) report suggests OpenAI may tie hardware sales to subscription plans and build a developer ecosystem around AI agents.


## Why OpenAI Needs Its Own Phone


This is not a hardware play for fun.[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai) 's entire business runs inside other people's platforms — Apple's iOS,[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) 's Android, and every browser. That means Apple and Google control permissions, background processing, sensor access, and default assistant slots. "By creating its own smartphone and hardware stack, OpenAI would be able to use AI in all kinds of features without restrictions,"[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/27/openai-could-be-making-a-phone-with-ai-agents-replacing-apps/) reported. Ming-Chi Kuo put it bluntly: "The smartphone is the only device that captures the user's full real-time state, which is the most important input for real-time[AI agent](https://opentools.ai/tools/ai-agent) inference. Only by fully controlling both the operating system and hardware can OpenAI deliver a complete AI agent service," as quoted in[EE Times](https://www.eetimes.com/openai-prepares-ai-first-smartphone-for-2028/) . Sam Altman acknowledged the pivot on X, noting that while OpenAI once believed it could disrupt the iPhone with a new device category, it now sees the smartphone as central to AI use for years to come.


## Timeline: Late 2027 or Bust


The clock is ticking. *Cailian Press* pegs market debut at **late 2027 or sometime in 2028** , according to[Gadgets360](https://www.gadgets360.com/mobiles/news/openai-ai-phone-assembly-manufacturing-partner-launch-timeline-report-12352522) . Earlier reports from Kuo suggested mass production could start in the first half of 2027, but supply chain timelines appear to have slipped. One wildcard: **Apple sued[OpenAI](https://opentools.ai/organizations/openai)** over alleged trade secret theft involving former employees who took confidential product development and supplier information. A federal judge granted Apple limited expedited discovery in October 2026,[Android Authority](https://www.androidauthority.com/openai-phone-foxconn-assembly-3737193/) reported. The lawsuit could slow hardware plans, but the fact that supply chain reports keep surfacing suggests the smartphone project is still moving.[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) and Samsung are already shipping agentic AI features on their own devices. OpenAI needs to ship before the window closes.
